# Example transcript: running s08 (the RepoMap).
#
# This output IS deterministic — there is no LLM call. The repo map is computed
# entirely locally from the source files (extract tags -> build graph ->
# PageRank -> fill a token budget). The numbers below come from a tiny 4-file
# sample repo:
#
#   store.go    defines Store, NewStore, Add, Count        (the central type)
#   cart.go     func Checkout(s *Store) { ... s.Count ... } (references Store)
#   report.go   func Report(s *Store)   { ... s.Add ...  }  (references Store)
#   unused.go   func Helper()                               (referenced by nobody)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Verbose mode: SEE the graph and the PageRank scores that drive the map.
#    Both cart.go and report.go point at store.go (they use its symbols), so
#    store.go is the most "central" file and earns the highest PageRank.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ go run . -dir ./sample -tokens 200 -v
[s08] scanned 4 files under ./sample, budget=200 tokens
[s08] dependency edges (referencer -> definer  weight):
    cart.go -> store.go  3.0
    report.go -> store.go  3.0
[s08] PageRank (higher = more central):
    0.4737  store.go
    0.1754  cart.go
    0.1754  report.go
    0.1754  unused.go
===== REPO MAP (budget=200 tokens, ~45 used) =====
cart.go:
  Checkout  (line 3)

report.go:
  Report  (line 3)

unused.go:
  Helper  (line 4)

store.go:
  Add  (line 8)
  Count  (line 10)
  NewStore  (line 6)
  Store  (line 4)

# NOTE: store.go has the highest *file* rank, but that rank is SPLIT across its
# four exported symbols, so each store.go symbol scores ~0.118 — below the
# single, unsplit symbols Checkout/Report/Helper (~0.175 each). We rank
# SYMBOLS, not files, so the lone-symbol files list first. A file whose ONE
# symbol is used everywhere (see Test 3's Core) concentrates all its rank and
# rises to the very top.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. A tight token budget keeps only the highest-ranked symbols. ~chars/4 is the
#    (deliberately lossy) token estimate; the budget is a soft cap — we stop
#    BEFORE exceeding it.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ go run . -dir ./sample -tokens 20
===== REPO MAP (budget=20 tokens, ~16 used) =====
cart.go:
  Checkout  (line 3)

report.go:
  Report  (line 3)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Put cart.go "in the chat" (-chat): PageRank's teleport vector concentrates
#    on cart.go, so what cart.go depends on (store.go) inherits more rank and
#    the map is reordered toward the code you are working on.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ go run . -dir ./sample -tokens 200 -chat cart.go
===== REPO MAP (budget=200 tokens, ~45 used) =====
cart.go:
  Checkout  (line 3)

store.go:
  Add  (line 8)
  Count  (line 10)
  NewStore  (line 6)
  Store  (line 4)

report.go:
  Report  (line 3)

unused.go:
  Helper  (line 4)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. -as-message shows EXACTLY how the loop (s01..s07) injects the map: a
#    read-only user turn prepended before the real instruction, so the model can
#    "see" a repo far too large to paste in full.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ go run . -dir ./sample -tokens 30 -as-message
===== READ-ONLY repo-map Message (role=user) =====
Here are summaries of files in my git repository.
Do not propose changes to these files, treat them as *read-only*.

cart.go:
  Checkout  (line 3)

report.go:
  Report  (line 3)

unused.go:
  Helper  (line 4)
